newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London quiet, HSBC gains.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London quiet, HSBC gains.

text.p: Another strong performance by banking group HSBC Holdings Plc was the standout feature on Tuesday in an otherwise quiet session for Hong Kong shares in London, dealers said.
HSBC Holdings gained HK$2.50 from its Hong Kong close to HK$207.50 by 1435 GMT, after earlier setting a record HK$207.90.
Dealers said the stock was dragged higher by a strong performance by the London registered stock and by arbitrage trade between the London registered shares and those registered in Hong Kong.
"It looks like there is selling of the ordinary (UK shares) and buying of the ten dollar (HK) stock," said one dealer.

In the broad market, the Hong Kong London Reference Index rose 10.53 points to 13,589.87, after the Hang Seng index posted its fifth consecutive advance following Wall Street's Monday rally. The Hang Seng index closed up 180 points, or 1.34 per cent, at 13,579.34.
Dealers said shares in London, with the exception of banks, stayed around their Hong Kong closing levels.
"I think investors are a little nervous with prices at these high levels," said one dealer.
